self.title: Can Information Be Scrambled Yet Still Leave Reliable Records?

detail.title: Information Scrambling and Record Accessibility
detail.summary: Scrambling (delocalization of quantum information) does not inherently prevent the formation of objective records. Objectivity is achieved when system pointer states are redundantly encoded into environmental degrees of freedom, a process formalized by Spectrum Broadcast Structures and clarified by the A/R/F framework's distinction between environmental and effective redundancy.
detail.reason: Incorporating A/R/F framework insights and SBS analysis into the scrambling project notebook to refine the understanding of redundant record formation.

detail.title: Information Scrambling and Record Accessibility Reconsidered
detail.summary: Information scrambling disperses quantum state information globally across complex degrees of freedom, whereas objective records require redundant local environmental encoding to allow independent observer access. Comparing quantum Darwinism, spectrum broadcast structures, and second-order free probability approaches reveals distinct operational limits on macroscopic objectivity.
detail.reason: Revising notebook nb-scrambling-records-01 with new evidence to characterize the relationship between global information scrambling and locally accessible objective records.
